claims.text: CFRP composites can provide lower weight than traditional metal alloys.
CFRP composites can provide superior overall performance compared with traditional metal alloys.
The proposed lightweight performance is attributable to CFRP's low density.
The proposed overall performance is attributable to CFRP's high strength-to-weight ratio.
The material consists of carbon fibers integrated within a polymer matrix.
The CFRP samples can be prepared by controlled layup or resin transfer molding.
Alignment of the carbon fibers is a structural mediator of performance.
Robust bonding between the carbon fibers and polymer matrix is a structural mediator of performance.
The polymer matrix efficiently transfers applied load to the carbon fibers.
The carbon fibers are high-strength reinforcements.
Efficient load transfer to the carbon fibers produces high mechanical performance while retaining low density.
CFRP components will weigh at least 10% less than comparable aluminum-alloy components.
CFRP will match or exceed the mechanical properties of baseline aluminum alloys.
The polymer matrix degrades at extremely high temperatures.
High-temperature polymer-matrix degradation reduces CFRP performance and limits its applicability in high-temperature environments.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies at least 10% lower component weight, whereas the falsification rule tests at least 10% lower density. Component weight and material density are not equivalent unless component geometry or functional equivalence is controlled.

The predicted outcome requires both a weight reduction and matched or superior mechanical properties, but the falsification rule is triggered only when both density reduction and mechanical performance fail. Failure of either individual predicted requirement would therefore not necessarily falsify the hypothesis.
